job.title: Infrastructure Planning Engineer
job.description:
Infrastructure Planning Engineer
Local Government | South Australia
Full-time | Permanent | Competitive salary + superannuation

Plan smarter infrastructure renewal
Our client is a progressive and well-established metropolitan council serving a diverse and growing community of more than 130,000 residents, the organisation manages a significant portfolio of community infrastructure, roads, drainage, open space and
public assets. They are seeking an experienced Infrastructure Planning Engineer to help shape this local Council’s future infrastructure renewal program.

This is a technically focused role for an engineer who can assess infrastructure condition, understand underlying failure mechanisms and develop practical, cost-effective renewal strategies. It is an opportunity to join a collaborative engineering environment where you can make a genuine contribution to the community by developing well investigated, integrated, appropriately budgeted and clearly scoped projects that the delivery teams can take forward.

• Professional development opportunities and career growth
• Utilise your technical depth to solve complex asset challenges
• Develop well investigated and clear project scopes for capital works

About the role
You will be responsible for:
• Planning and scoping renewal projects across roads, pavements, curb and gutter, footpaths and stormwater infrastructure.
• Reviewing asset condition, maintenance history, traffic, drainage and existing infrastructure information.
• Developing and managing appropriate site investigations and structural assessments.
• Diagnosing pavement and infrastructure deterioration and determining appropriate rehabilitation treatments.
• Identifying opportunities to coordinate road works with drainage, utilities, footpaths, accessibility, curb and streetscape improvements.
• Preparing project scopes, technical briefs, preliminary cost estimates, risk assessments and business cases.
• Working closely with asset management, design, delivery, operations, consultants and other stakeholders.
• Applying whole-of-life asset management principles to optimise investment and minimise future maintenance and rework.

About you
You will be a qualified Civil Engineer with demonstrated experience in infrastructure planning, asset management, road rehabilitation or civil project scoping development.

You will ideally bring:
• Strong pavement engineering and road rehabilitation knowledge.
• Experience investigating infrastructure failures and interpreting technical testing.
• Understanding of stormwater, drainage and civil infrastructure interfaces.
• A curiosity for alternative materials, treatments and approaches and identify opportunities to improve asset life and environmental impacts.
• Experience developing renewal scopes and treatment strategies.
• Strong analytical, communication and stakeholder management skills.
• A practical understanding of construction, risk, cost and whole-of-life considerations.

Local government experience is desirable, but we also welcome candidates from consulting or infrastructure delivery backgrounds.

Why join?
This is an opportunity to influence infrastructure investment before projects reach detailed design and construction — ensuring Council delivers the right treatment, in the right location, at the right time.

This is a full-time permanent opportunity offering competitive remuneration and the opportunity to join a dynamic environment, shaping the future of our City.

If you enjoy solving complex infrastructure problems, challenging assumptions and turning asset information into practical renewal project scopes, we would like to hear from you.

Keen to learn more before applying?

job.title: Development Property Manager
job.description:
Role Summary

The Development Project Manager – Apartments is responsible for the client-side management and delivery of medium density residential developments across the Rent to Own program. The role leads projects through all phases of the development lifecycle, including site feasibility, planning and approvals, procurement, design management, stakeholder engagement, construction delivery and project close-out. Working within a multi-disciplinary development team, the incumbent will manage several projects simultaneously and be accountable for ensuring projects achieve commercial, program, quality, social and customer outcomes. The role requires strong development management capability, strategic thinking and stakeholder management skills to successfully deliver complex townhouse and apartment developments.

Primary Outcomes and Responsibilities

Development Management

  • Lead the end-to-end delivery of medium density residential developments from project inception through to completion.
  • Manage development feasibility, business case development and project establishment activities.
  • Develop and maintain project delivery strategies, programs and budgets.
  • Identify and manage project risks, opportunities and dependencies throughout the development lifecycle.
  • Monitor project performance against approved scope, budget, quality and time objectives.

Design and Planning Leadership

  • Manage consultant teams including architects, planners, engineers, surveyors and specialist advisers.
  • Coordinate and oversee preparation of development concepts, design documentation and approval submissions.
  • Ensure developments achieve planning, urban design, customer, sustainability and housing policy objectives.
  • Lead resolution of design, planning and stakeholder issues to maintain project progress.
  • Promote innovation and continuous improvement in project design and delivery outcomes.

Procurement and Commercial Management

  • Manage procurement processes for consultants, development partners and builders in accordance with Government procurement requirements.
  • Prepare procurement documentation, evaluation reports and approval briefings.
  • Monitor project budgets, cost forecasts and financial performance.
  • Assess variations, claims and commercial matters in accordance with contractual obligations and delegated authority.
  • Contribute to continuous improvement of development delivery frameworks and procurement approaches.

Stakeholder and Partnership Management

  • Establish and maintain productive relationships with internal and external stakeholders.
  • Engage effectively with local government, State Government agencies, industry representatives and community stakeholders.
  • Work collaboratively with development partners, consultants and builders to support successful project outcomes.
  • Prepare high-quality ministerial briefings, executive reports, presentations and project updates.

Construction and Delivery Oversight

  • Monitor construction delivery activities to ensure projects achieve approved scope, quality, program and budget outcomes.
  • Work collaboratively with appointed builders and consultants to address delivery issues and project risks.
  • Review project performance reporting and support timely resolution of construction-related matters.
  • Facilitate project handover, defects management and close-out activities.

Strategic Contribution

  • Provide specialist development management advice to support the delivery of the Housing Trust's strategic objectives.
  • Contribute to program planning, pipeline development and portfolio reporting activities.
  • Support the identification and implementation of opportunities to improve housing delivery outcomes and value for money.

Selection Criteria

Essential Knowledge and Experience

  • Demonstrated experience managing residential development projects through planning, design and delivery phases.
  • Experience managing multiple projects simultaneously within complex stakeholder environments.
  • Strong understanding of South Australia's planning and development system.
  • Experience managing project budgets, procurement processes, contracts and commercial risks.
  • Proven ability to establish and maintain productive relationships with government agencies, consultants, industry partners and community stakeholders.
  • Experience preparing executive reports, briefing papers and recommendations.

Desirable Knowledge and Experience

  • Experience delivering medium density residential developments including townhouses and apartment projects.
  • Knowledge of affordable housing, social housing or build-to-rent development models.
  • Experience working within government, urban renewal, residential development or client-side project management environments.
  • Understanding of construction delivery, building contracts and project commissioning processes.

Capability Requirements

  • Strong project and program management capability.
  • Commercial and financial acumen.
  • Strategic thinking and problem-solving skills.
  • High-level negotiation and stakeholder engagement skills.
  • Excellent written and verbal communication skills.
  • Ability to influence outcomes and drive projects to completion.

Qualifications (desirable)

Degree qualification in one or more of the following:

  • Property Development
  • Urban and Regional Planning
  • Construction Management
  • Project Management
  • Architecture
  • Civil Engineering
  • Property Economics
  • Quantity Surveying
  • Equivalent discipline

job.title: Chief Executive Officer
job.description:
Harrison McMillan has the privilege of partnering with Hepatitis SA to appoint their next Chief Executive Officer.

About Hepatitis SA
Hepatitis SA is the lead community-based, not-for-profit organisation responding to viral hepatitis, primarily hepatitis B and hepatitis C, in South Australia.

The organisation provides education, peer education, information, referral and support services for people affected by viral hepatitis, people at risk, health and welfare professionals, and the broader community. Hepatitis SA is also a Needle and Syringe Program secondary site and operates harm reduction peer services across various NSP sites in metropolitan Adelaide.

With a committed team, strong sector relationships and a community-led approach, Hepatitis SA plays an important role in public health, harm reduction, advocacy and providing services for priority populations.

About the role
Reporting to the Board, the CEO will lead the day-to-day management and implementation of the strategic direction of Hepatitis SA.

This is a broad, hands-on role spanning service delivery, advocacy, funding and financial management, people management and stakeholder engagement, and advising the Board on policy, strategic and operational direction, organisational risk and finances.

The incoming CEO will build on strong organisational foundations while strengthening funding sustainability, systems and processes and impact reporting

Key Responsibilities:
  • Lead Hepatitis SA’s operations, programs and people
  • Ensure services remain responsive to communities affected by viral hepatitis
  • Oversee education, peer education, support and harm reduction programs
  • Manage budgets, grants, funding submissions, acquittals, tenders and reporting
  • Build strong relationships with funders, government, sector partners and community stakeholders
  • Represent Hepatitis SA in local, state and national forums
  • Advise the Board re strategy, governance, risk, and budget planning and monitoring
  • Lead and support a small, diverse team, including peer workers
  • Strengthen systems, policies, documentation and organisational processes
  • Communicate the impact of Hepatitis SA’s work to funders, partners and the broader community

What we’re looking for:
  • Experience: Senior leadership experience in health, human services, community, not-for-profit or related settings
  • Financial Capability: Strong skills in budgeting, grants, acquittals, funding reports and tenders
  • Governance Knowledge: Experience working effectively with a Board
  • Community Understanding: Appreciation of health promotion, harm reduction lived experience and peer-led programs
  • Ability to Navigate Complexity: Comfortable operating in challenging environments with the ability to work autonomously, exercise sound judgement, and navigate complexity with confidence.
  • Communication: Strong written and verbal communication skills
  • Leadership Style: Practical, inclusive, non-judgemental and able to build trust with diverse communities
  • Flexibility: Ability to work flexibly and undertake some intrastate and interstate travel

Benefits:
  • Meaningful Impact: Lead work that directly supports people affected by viral hepatitis
  • Strong Foundations: Join a respected organisation with experienced staff and sector relationships
  • Sector Influence: Represent Hepatitis SA across local, state and national forums
  • Purpose-Led Work: Contribute to hepatitis B and C elimination goals, with a focus on equity and no-one left behind
  • Salary Packaging: Salary packaging arrangements are available
  • Flexible Working: WFH options may apply after the first 12 months, subject to performance and policy

Why join Hepatitis SA?
This is an opportunity to lead a respected, community-based organisation with deep community connections and an important role in South Australia’s public health landscape.

The coming years will be important for Hepatitis SA, with new National Strategies, a changing funding environment, ongoing advocacy and continued work toward the elimination of hepatitis B and hepatitis C as public health threats.

This role will suit a leader who is both strategic and practical; someone who can build on what is already working well while strengthening and evolving the organisation for the future.

job.description:
Join a high performing team delivering complex defence projects, owning document control, driving consistency and shaping how information flows.

  • Work at the centre of major projects where detail and pace matter
  • Own critical workflows and keep complex project information moving
  • Collaborative team, strong leadership and a 9-day fortnight

About the Company

Australian Naval Infrastructure (ANI) plays a critical role in supporting Australia’s naval shipbuilding enterprise and managing nationally significant defence infrastructure. Based in Adelaide, ANI is responsible for delivering and managing infrastructure that supports the long-term development of Australia’s naval capability. This is an opportunity to join a high performing project and infrastructure environment supporting nationally significant defence programs.

Role Overview

This is a senior level Document Controller role operating at the centre of major defence infrastructure delivery. You will take ownership of document control systems and workflows, ensuring complete accuracy, traceability, and compliance across all project documentation. This is not a transactional role, it is a governance focused position where your control of information directly supports program delivery and assurance. You will work across multiple stakeholders in a structured, high accountability environment where precision and discipline are essential. You will be operating in a fast paced, high-volume environment, managing multiple workflows and stakeholders concurrently while working to tight project timeframes. This is an opportunity to join a growing, well-structured team where you contribute to process improvement and play a key role in supporting major project delivery.

You are an established Document Controller with strong experience in large scale infrastructure, engineering, or defence environments. You are confident operating within structured systems and understand the importance of strict process adherence in regulated project settings. You are calm under pressure, highly methodical, and trusted to operate effectively in complex, high volume environments. You ideally bring strong Aconex capability and are comfortable being the “gatekeeper” of accuracy, consistency, and compliance. You can step into an established environment and quickly get up to speed, operating with minimal direction.

Key Responsibilities

  • Own document control governance across major defence infrastructure programs
  • Manage workflows, transmittals, submissions, and structured review cycles
  • Maintain document registers, numbering systems, and version control integrity
  • Ensure compliance with strict governance, audit, and project assurance requirements
  • Monitor and report on document status, workflow performance, and delivery progress
  • Assist with onboarding and capability uplift of new users across the program
  • Maintain discipline, accuracy, and consistency across all document control activity

  • Australian citizenship is essential due to defence security requirements
  • Experience within major infrastructure, engineering or construction projects is essential
  • Strong Aconex (or equivalent) experience is highly regarded
  • Strong exposure to complex, regulated project environments
  • Deep understanding of document governance, compliance, and audit requirements
  • Proven ability to manage high volume workflows with absolute accuracy
  • Strong stakeholder engagement across technical and project delivery teams
  • Confident working independently within structured environments
